speaker: Sarah
text: Can everyone hear me? Okay. Q2 pipeline review. We have forty-five minutes.

speaker: Tom
text: Can you see my screen? The numbers are up.

speaker: Sarah
text: Yes. Start with revenue, then pricing, then hiring.

speaker: Tom
text: Closed Q1 at one point two four million ARR, up eleven percent quarter over quarter.

speaker: Tom
text: Closed Q1 at one point two four million ARR, up eleven percent quarter over quarter. Net revenue retention is one hundred four percent. Logo churn is three point one percent, up from two point four.

speaker: Priya
text: Pipeline is four hundred eighty thousand weighted, but one hundred ninety thousand of that is Acme and it is stuck in security review.

speaker: Sarah
text: Stuck how?

speaker: Priya
text: Their CISO wants SSO and a DPA with EU data residency before they sign. Legal has had the DPA for three weeks.

speaker: Marcus
text: SSO is roughly four weeks of work if we drop the audit log polish. We cannot do both by May.

speaker: Sarah
text: That is a real tradeoff. What does the audit log buy us?

speaker: Marcus
text: Two renewals in June, about ninety thousand ARR. Acme is one hundred ninety.

speaker: Tom
text: Acme is also the eighteen-month term. I would prioritize Acme.

speaker: Priya
text: Agreed. But if we slip the audit log I need something for those two renewals.

speaker: Sarah
text: Decision: SSO first, audit log moves to June. Marcus, confirm the four-week estimate by Wednesday.

speaker: Marcus
text: Will do.

speaker: Sarah
text: Sorry, that is my dog. Ignore the barking.

speaker: Priya
text: Back to pricing. Tom, the model says we are leaving money on the table.

speaker: Tom
text: We have not raised list price in two years. An eight percent increase on new logos adds about one hundred forty thousand ARR next year. Churn risk is maybe half a point.

speaker: Priya
text: Sales can absorb eight percent if we grandfather existing customers for twelve months. Anything more and I lose the mid-market deals.

speaker: Sarah
text: Decision: eight percent list increase for new customers from May first. Existing customers grandfathered for twelve months. Priya, pricing FAQ to the sales team by Friday.

speaker: Priya
text: Friday is tight with the Acme call, but yes.

speaker: Tom
text: I will update the forecast model with the new price and the churn assumption by Monday.

speaker: Sarah
text: Hiring. We have two open AE reqs and one engineer backfill.

speaker: Priya
text: I need both AEs. Pipeline coverage is two point one x. We need three x.

speaker: Tom
text: I would freeze the AEs until we see Q2. Two AEs is two hundred eighty thousand fully loaded. That is the entire pricing upside.

speaker: Priya
text: If we do not hire, we miss the number. It is not discretionary.

speaker: Tom
text: Tom, you are on mute. Sorry.

speaker: Sarah
text: We are not going to settle this with vibes. Decision: hire one AE now, hold the second until the June review. Keep the engineer backfill.

speaker: Marcus
text: Engineering is already at eighty-five percent utilization. The backfill is needed regardless.

speaker: Sarah
text: Keep it. One AE, one engineer backfill, second AE deferred.

speaker: Tom
text: I will model both hiring scenarios so we can see the trigger for the second AE.

speaker: Sarah
text: Open question: do we change the free tier? I do not want to decide that today.

speaker: Priya
text: Let us take it offline.

speaker: Sarah
text: Anything else?

speaker: Marcus
text: The EU data residency question from Acme is not just a DPA. We would need a Frankfurt region. That is a quarter, not a sprint.

speaker: Sarah
text: That is a risk we have not priced. Tom, can you cost a Frankfurt region?

speaker: Tom
text: Rough number by next week.

speaker: Sarah
text: Good. Recap. SSO first, audit log June. Eight percent new-customer price from May first, grandfather twelve months. One AE now, second at the June review, engineer backfill approved. Acme depends on SSO plus the DPA. Frankfurt is an open risk.

speaker: Sarah
text: Owners: Marcus SSO estimate Wednesday. Priya pricing FAQ Friday. Tom forecast Monday and Frankfurt cost next week.

speaker: Priya
text: That is right.
